newsitem.title: USA: PECO set to take stake in Louisiana nuke.
newsitem.headline: PECO set to take stake in Louisiana nuke.

text.p: PECO Energy Co, the Philadelphia-based power utility, said Thursday it took a major step toward acquiring a 30 percent stake in the Riverbend nuclear power station in Louisiana.
PECO's $50 million bid for a stake in the 936 megawatt plant, filed in February, was approved last week by the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Baton Rouge, La., the company said.

"This means we're free to proceed. We are doing due diligence, checking to make sure the numbers add up. We don't foresee any problems and hope to have everything wrapped up by the end of the year," said PECO spokesman Bill Jones.

PECO Power Team, the utility's bulk electricity marketing arm, signed the agreement with the Rural Utilities Service (RUS) and the trustee for Cajun Electric Power Cooperative, which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in late 1994.
RUS lent the money to Cajun to build the plant, which began commercial operation in 1986, and took control of Cajun's Riverbend share as part of its bankruptcy settlement with Cajun.
Riverbend, in St Francisville, La., is operated by New Orleans-based Entergy Corp, who also own the remaining 70 percent.
This will be Entergy's first partnership with PECO.
